newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-EUROPEAN CHAMPIONS HIT BY STRUNZ ILLNESS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EUROPEAN CHAMPIONS HIT BY STRUNZ ILLNESS.

text.p: Germany's squad for this weekend's difficult World Cup qualifier in Portugal was hit by another withdrawal on Tuesday when key Bayern Munich midfielder Thomas Strunz pulled out with influenza.

Euro 96 player Strunz missed Bayern's final league game before the winter break at the weekend and told coach Berti Vogts he would not be able to travel with the party to Lisbon for Saturday's European group nine clash.

The late withdrawal is a blow to the European champions who will also be missing midfielders Mehmet Scholl and Thomas Haessler, defender Thomas Helmer, reserve goalkeeper Oliver Kahn and striker Oliver Bierhoff, hero of the Euro 96 final.
The party, which is due to fly to Portugal on Thursday, has been reduced to 19.
The Portuguese have a special place in the history of German football. They are the only team ever to have beaten the Germans in a World Cup qualifier, winning 1-0 in Stuttgart in October 1985.
The Germans have not lost to the Portuguese since and beat them 2-1 in a friendly in Porto in February.
But Vogts said: "We were in good shape then. When I see how Porto have marched through the Champions' League, I'm not so sure that we can travel to Lisbon with so much optimism this time."
Libero Matthias Sammer and wing-back Christian Ziege, who missed the European champions frustrating 1-1 draw at home to Northern Ireland last month, were fit to join the squad on Tuesday.
Bayern Munich's in-form midfielder Mario Basler, who was part of the Euro 96 squad but did not make an impact because of injury, can now expect to be given an important role in midfield.

Bayer Leverkusen striker Ulf Kirsten's superb form in the first half of the season has been rewarded with a place in the squad but VfB Stuttgart's Fredi Bobic is expected to join captain Juergen Klinsmann up front.
Goalkeepers: Andreas Koepke (Marseille), Oliver Reck (Werder Bremen)
Defenders: Markus Babbel (Bayern Munich), Juergen Kohler, Stefan Reuter, Matthias Sammer (all Borussia Dortmund), Christian Woerns (Bayer Leverkusen)

Midfielders: Mario Basler (Bayern), Marco Bode, Dieter Eilts (both Werder Bremen), Joerg Heinrich, Andy Moeller (both Dortmund), Michael Tarnat (Karlsruhe), Dariusz Wosz (Bochum), Christian Ziege (Bayern)
Forwards: Fredi Bobic (Stuttgart), Heiko Herrlich (Dortmund), Ulf Kirsten (Leverkusen), Juergen Klinsmann (Bayern)
